result.topic_en: Gauss finishes a proof that the coefficients of the series for the reciprocal of the arithmetic-geometric mean are A=1/4, B=1/4·9/16, etc., and then shows that this series satisfies a second-order linear differential equation.

8. Si statuimus $1+\frac{1}{4}xx+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}x^4+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}.\frac{25}{36}x^6+$ etc. $=y$, fit
$\frac{1}{2}xx+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{4}x^4+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}.\frac{25}{6}x^6+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}.\frac{25}{36}.\frac{49}{8}x^8+$ etc. $=\frac{xdy}{dx}$ atque
$xx+\frac{1}{4}.9x^4+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}.25x^6+\frac{1}{4}.\frac{9}{16}.\frac{25}{36}.49x^8+$ etc. $=\frac{xxddy}{dx^2}+\frac{xdy}{dx}$, unde
sponte sequitur $\frac{xxddy}{dx^2}+3\frac{xdy}{dx}+y=\frac{1}{xx}\left(xx\frac{ddy}{dx^2}+\frac{xdy}{dx}\right)$ sive
$(x^3-x)\frac{ddy}{dx^2}+(3xx-1)\frac{dy}{dx}+xy=0$. Hoc itaque modo media nostra arithmetico-geometrica ad quantitates integrales revocata sunt, solutionemque particularem huiusce aequationis differentio-differentialis suppeditant.
Eiusdem aequationis int. compl. est $\frac{2}{M(1+x,1-x)}$ [?] + [illegible]

methods.what: Recursive system of linear equations for the series coefficients A, B, C, ...
General n-th equation of the system, with binomial-type coefficients
Solution of the system: the coefficients are products of squared ratios of odd to even numbers
Series for the reciprocal of the AGM and the differential equation it satisfies (complete elliptic integral / hypergeometric ODE)
Term-by-term differentiation of the series to derive the ODE
